channel.description: I'm a British Inventor and Engineer who loves problem solving, learning new skills and making crazy inventions! One half of Kids Invent Stuff- www.youtube.com/kidsinventstuff

videos.t: Building my Dream Workshop!
videos.desc:
I built my own workshop from scratch in my back garden, loosely based on Colin Furze's award winning workshop. Technically a glorified shed, the workshop is 3.7m by 3.7m and I love it! 

You can find some of my other content over at Kids Invent Stuff (https://www.youtube.com/kidsinventstuff ) where I bring to life kids’ invention ideas with my friend Shawn.

Instructables write up- https://www.instructables.com/Building-My-Dream-Workshop/

Help support my work and stay up to date with everything im making- https://www.patreon.com/IamRuthAmos

videos.t: 🚨 Inventors, read this before you share your idea online!
videos.desc:
In the UK, Europe, and most of the world, any public disclosure—yes, even a school talk or an Instagram post—can kill your chances of getting a patent. 💀

Unless you’ve filed first, your idea is no longer “novel,” and that means it’s no longer protectable.

🇺🇸 The US gives you a 12-month grace period, but most countries don’t. No second chances.

🧠 Moral of the story? File before you share.

#InventorTips #PatentMistakes #ProtectYourIdea #STEM #Makers #EngineeringLife #Innovation #IdeaToReality

videos.t: This week I got that new-tool feeling...
videos.desc:
... thanks to @machinemartuk who kindly sent a few things over. #Gifted
And it got me thinking.
The excitement of opening something new is never just about the tool. It is about the shelves that stop the clutter, the jig that saves you ten minutes every time, the gift you make for someone you love. It is about the patience, the problem-solving, the tiny moments in between where an idea becomes something real.
So here’s to the things we create, and the tools that help us get there.
Thank you Machine Mart for the new additions to the workshop, they’ve already sparked a dozen ideas.
#MakerLife #D

videos.t: Some people inherit money, Vansittart inherited an engineering problem. ⚙️🚢
videos.desc:
When her father died, he left behind years of work trying to improve the ship’s propeller. But Henrietta wasn’t about to let his work go unfinished.
She took on the challenge, developed the design further and became a pioneering female inventor in a world that rarely made space for women in engineering.

Proof that sometimes the most interesting family inheritance is a problem waiting to be solved. 💙
#HerStory #WomenInEngineering #WomenInSTEM #Inventors #EngineeringHistory

videos.t: Imagine your computer crashing while landing on the moon 🌙
videos.desc:
You might know the names Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, but do you know Margaret Hamilton? 🚀🌕

While the world watched humans land on the Moon, Margaret and her team had written the software that helped make it possible.

She understood something incredibly important: great engineering isn’t about making sure nothing ever goes wrong. It’s about planning for when it does.

Her work helped change the future of software engineering, and her legacy is a reminder that some of the most extraordinary achievements in history are made possible by people whose names we don’t always know.

Here’s to Mar
